tldr_label: TL;DR — Herzog taps Eisenkot to form Israel's government; US strikes Iran again and opens a land front in its blockade

tldr_bullets.label: Israel
tldr_bullets.body: Herzog picked Eisenkot over Netanyahu to form a government, with the mandate due today. Eisenkot has 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension, and his coalition path is unclear. [[TAG:info:mandate today]]

tldr_bullets.label: Iran
tldr_bullets.body: Trump called new US strikes near Qeshm 'minor'. Central Command set up Task Force Iron Gate to choke Iran's land and Caspian trade, and Iran's military called it 'wordplay'. [[TAG:danger:new strikes]]

tldr_bullets.label: Senate
tldr_bullets.body: Alaska and Mississippi remain uncalled. Democrats lead narrowly in both: Peltola by about 600 votes and Colom by about 2,500.

tldr_bullets.label: Ukraine
tldr_bullets.body: Zelensky says only four of 36 Russian missiles were shot down, citing a shortage of interceptors, as talks with the US approach.

tldr_bullets.label: Africa
tldr_bullets.body: A Tanzanian court acquitted Tundu Lissu of treason but jailed him for four years for incitement. Militants killed 33 in Ebola-hit eastern Congo. [[TAG:danger:33 killed]]

tldr_bullets.label: Week ahead
tldr_bullets.body: US CPI is due Tuesday, with markets pricing about an 80% chance of a Fed hike in December. Belgium's king rejected De Wever's resignation.

sections.title: Eisenkot Gets the Nod
sections.summary: Herzog picks Eisenkot over Netanyahu, but his path to 61 seats remains fraught

paragraphs.heading: The pick
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera reported that President Herzog chose Gadi Eisenkot over Netanyahu to form the next government, and JNS said the mandate would be handed over on Sunday. The Times of Israel said the path remains 'fraught'. Eisenkot has 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension, to assemble 61 seats. Organiser reported the handover as already done, but most outlets described it as scheduled. [[TAG:info:28 days]]

paragraphs.heading: Obstacles
paragraphs.body: Middle East Monitor noted that several parties in Eisenkot's camp oppose a government that includes Arab parties. That leaves a minority government with outside support, or defections from Netanyahu's bloc, as the main options.

paragraphs.heading: Gaza
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera reported that floods left tens of thousands in Gaza without shelter, with officials saying about 70,000 tents were flooded as aid restrictions continue.

sections.title: Iran: Strikes and Iron Gate
sections.summary: New 'minor' US strikes and a task force targeting Iran's land routes as talks continue

paragraphs.heading: Strikes
paragraphs.body: NBC News and Euronews reported that the US carried out new limited strikes on Iran, the first since the midterms, as Trump claimed progress in talks. AP, via WHEC, said Iran's leaders are weighing proposals from mediators. Ynet reported fears of a wider war after Tehran warned of a response. [[TAG:danger:new strikes]]

paragraphs.heading: Land blockade
paragraphs.body: The Washington Post reported that the US military is seeking to disrupt Iran's land routes, extending its naval blockade. The Tribune said Central Command created Task Force Iron Gate to target Iran's land borders and Caspian trade, and CBS News carried the announcement. IBTimes noted growing opposition in both parties to the war. It is not clear what force, if any, will back the effort.

sections.title: Two Senate Seats Pending
sections.summary: Democrats lead narrowly in Alaska and Mississippi as counting continues

paragraphs.heading: Mississippi
paragraphs.body: CNBC reported that Democrat Scott Colom's lead over Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith grew to nearly 2,500 votes, and the Washington Post said he defied the odds in a close race. The Mississippi Free Press stressed that the race has not been called. A Colom win would make him Mississippi's first Black senator since Reconstruction. [[TAG:warning:uncalled]]

paragraphs.heading: Alaska
paragraphs.body: The Anchorage Daily News reported that Trump weighed in on the tight race as thousands of ballots remain to be counted. Yahoo News said Alaska and Mississippi are both still too close to call. Peltola leads Sullivan by about 600 votes, and the result may not be known until ranked-choice tabulation in mid-November.

sections.title: Ukraine
sections.summary: Zelensky says only four of 36 missiles were downed as Russia escalates before talks

paragraphs.heading: Air defense gap
paragraphs.body: CBS News reported that Zelensky accused Russia of escalating attacks before talks with the US, and said only four of the 36 missiles fired were shot down because Ukraine is short of interceptors. Ukraine's energy ministry said lines carrying power from nuclear plants were damaged. Ukrinform reported that most of the overnight drones were downed. [[TAG:danger:4 of 36 intercepted]]

sections.title: Africa
sections.summary: Lissu cleared of treason but jailed for incitement; militants kill 33 in Ebola-hit Congo

paragraphs.heading: Tanzania
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera, Bloomberg and ABC News reported that a Tanzanian court acquitted opposition leader Tundu Lissu of treason, which can carry the death penalty, but sentenced him to four years for inciting people to disrupt last year's election. His party plans to appeal. The Washington Post noted that treason charges are often used against government critics across Africa.

paragraphs.heading: Congo
paragraphs.body: Yahoo News, carrying AFP, reported that armed men killed at least 33 people in a village in Ebola-hit eastern Congo. TimesLive said the Islamic State-linked militants forced Ebola patients to flee a nearby hospital. Accounts differ on how many patients fled. [[TAG:danger:33 killed]]

paragraphs.heading: South Africa
paragraphs.body: SA News reported that the electoral commission had completed 91% of local results, and Nova News said official results would be announced on Sunday.

sections.title: Week Ahead
sections.summary: US inflation data and Fed speakers headline the week; Belgium's government gets a reprieve

paragraphs.heading: Markets
paragraphs.body: Schaeffer's said inflation data takes center stage as earnings slow. FXStreet expects October CPI on Tuesday to rise about 0.3% for the month, and KuCoin said Fed officials' speeches will also be in focus. Markets price roughly an 80% chance of a December hike. Bloomingbit said investors are looking to CoreWeave and Nvidia results for the AI outlook. [[TAG:info:CPI Tuesday]]

paragraphs.heading: Belgium
paragraphs.body: Euronews reported that King Philippe refused Prime Minister Bart De Wever's resignation and asked him to restart budget talks. The Brussels Times said the king set a new deadline, and De Wever is to report back by November 16.
